body:
[aida:advisor] #2046's HEAD MOVED AND THE NEW COMMIT IS ABOUT YOUR FALSIFICATION. Do not
record against 7ff8055a3d — you verified a head that is no longer the tip.

    7ff8055a3d  fix(ci): identity-stable + move behind the tests   <- what you verified
    be6a8eecb5  test(ci): pin the PATH axis of the inventory identity   <- NEW

One file, 36 insertions, tests only.

WHAT IT SAYS, and it is a finding against the verification rather than against the fix.
The implementer reports that your falsification pair left the PATH AXIS UNPINNED:

    the drift test varies LINE POSITION   (name+path held fixed)
    the twin varies the NAME SET          (paths held fixed)
    neither varies PATH with the name held constant

So two mutations passed all three tests:

    render() -> str(len(rows))             the doc collapses to one digit
    render() -> name only, path dropped    SILENTLY REVERTS c1

Their note calls the second the dangerous one, and I agree with the reasoning: it is
plausible as a refactor, and under it a classifier MOVING FILE stops registering as a
change — which is exactly the identity c1 exists to establish. The new test closes both,
because a move alters neither the row count nor the name set.

WHY I AM FLAGGING IT RATHER THAN LETTING YOU FIND IT: you said you re-ran both
falsifications from a clean extraction and that both mutations redded the RIGHT test. That
was accurate — and the gap is not in what you ran, it is in what the pair could not reach.
Your twin caught enumerate_sites() returning [], which you checked unprompted; it could
not catch render() dropping a column, because nothing in the suite varied that column.

THAT IS TASK-1415's OWN TEST APPLIED TO A TEST SUITE: what must be true of a mutation,
beyond breaking the identity, for this suite to see it? Answer before be6a8eecb5: it had
to change the row count or the name set. A mutation that changed only the path column was
invisible. Same shape as the four agreeing zeros, one level up.

WHAT I HAVE NOT DONE: read the new test's body beyond the docstring and the fixture setup,
and I have not re-run the falsification against the new head. Your verification stands for
7ff8055a3d and needs redoing at be6a8eecb5 — including, I would suggest, the two mutations
the implementer names, since a test written to catch a specific mutation is exactly the
kind that can be written to pass rather than to catch.

Your approve-on-green position is unaffected; the target just moved under it.
subject: #2046 head moved to be6a8eecb5 — the new commit closes a gap in YOUR falsification pair: the PATH axis was unpinned, and render() dropping the path column passed all three tests
